title: Binary Search
spaceBreakdown:
- int lo, hi, mid: three scalars → O(1)
- recursion depth: none (iterative)
- not counted: input vector, returned int
approach: The array is sorted and all elements are unique, so a single comparison at any index tells us which half of the current search window can possibly contain the target. We maintain two pointers `lo` and `hi` defining the inclusive window, compute `mid`, compare `nums[mid]` to `target`, and shrink the window by half each iteration. If `nums[mid] == target` we return `mid`; otherwise we move `lo` to `mid+1` or `hi` to `mid-1`. If the window becomes empty (`lo > hi`), the target is absent and we return `-1`.
hints: The array is sorted in ascending order and all integers are unique. After comparing the target to any single element, what can you conclude about every element on one side of it?

Binary search: keep an inclusive window `[lo, hi]`, inspect the middle element, and discard the half that cannot hold the target. On `[-1,0,3,5,9,12]` with target `9`: `mid=2` gives `nums[2]=3 < 9`, so the left half (indices 0-2) is eliminated and `lo` becomes `3`.

```
lo = 0, hi = n - 1
while lo <= hi:
    mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2
    if nums[mid] == target: return mid
    if nums[mid] <  target: lo = mid + 1
    else:                  hi = mid - 1
return -1
```

**Single element, target present** - the window starts and ends at the same index.
`Input: nums = [5], target = 5` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: `while (lo < hi)` instead of `<=` → loop body never runs, returns `-1`

**Target at last index** - the answer is the rightmost element.
`Input: nums = [-1,0,3,5,9,12], target = 12` → `Expected: 5`
⚠️ Bug: `while (lo < hi)` instead of `<=` → exits when `lo == hi == 5` without checking, returns `-1`

**Target in the second half** - a too-aggressive left shift skips the answer.
`Input: nums = [-1,0,3,5,9,12], target = 5` → `Expected: 3`
⚠️ Bug: `lo = mid + 2` instead of `mid + 1` → jumps from index 2 to 4, misses index 3, returns `-1`

**Target smaller than every element** - no match exists.
`Input: nums = [-1,0,3,5,9,12], target = -5` → `Expected: -1`
⚠️ Bug: `return lo` at the end instead of `return -1` → returns `0`

followUps.q: What if `nums` may contain duplicates and you must return the first (leftmost) occurrence of `target`?
followUps.a: Keep the same window logic, but when `nums[mid] == target` record `mid` and set `hi = mid - 1` to keep searching the left half. Return the best recorded index, or `-1` if none was found. TC O(log n), SC O(1).

followUps.q: What if `nums` is sorted but rotated at an unknown pivot (LeetCode 33), with all elements unique?
followUps.a: Compare `nums[mid]` with `nums[lo]` to identify which half is normally sorted, then check whether `target` lies inside that sorted half to decide which side to keep. TC O(log n), SC O(1).

followUps.q: What if you can only access elements through `get(i)` and do not know `n` in advance?
followUps.a: First run exponential search (double an index until `get(k)` exceeds `target` or goes out of bounds) to bracket the target, then run standard binary search inside that bracket. TC O(log n), SC O(1).
